'''Frank Curtis Michel''' (June 5, 1934 – February 26, 2015) was an American [[astrophysicist]]; a professor of astrophysics at [[Rice University]] in Houston, Texas; a [[United States Air Force]] [[Aviator|pilot]]; and a [[NASA astronaut]].

== Personal life ==
Michel was born June 5, 1934, to parents to Frank and Viola Michel. He was married to Bonnie Hausman, a web technical specialist. He had two children, Alice and Jeff with his first wife Beverly, who preceded him in death, and three grandchildren.<ref name=r1/> His hobbies were [[photography]], [[tennis]], [[American handball|handball]], and [[baseball]].<ref name=r2>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/michel-fc.pdf |title=Biographical Data: F. CURTIS MICHEL, NASA ASTRONAUT (DECEASED)|access-date=April 14, 2021|publisher=NASA|date=April 2015}} {{PD-notice}}</ref> Michel died at the age of 80 on February 26, 2015.<ref name=r1>{{cite web|url=http://news.rice.edu/2015/02/27/professor-emeritus-curt-michel-dies/|title=Professor emeritus Curt Michel dies|date=February 27, 2015|access-date=July 5, 2016|publisher=Rice University|archive-date=July 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706035804/http://news.rice.edu/2015/02/27/professor-emeritus-curt-michel-dies/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was buried with full [[Military funerals in the United States|military honors]] at the [[Houston National Cemetery]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?pid=174408818/ |title=Michel's burial|publisher=Legacy|access-date=September 7, 2016}}</ref>

== Education ==
Michel graduated from [[C. K. McClatchy High School]], located at [[Sacramento, California]], in 1951. In 1955, he received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree with honors in [[physics]], and in 1962 he received a [[doctorate]] in [[physics]], both from the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref name=r2/> His thesis was ''"Beta Spectra of the Mass 12 Nuclei"'' and his dissertation advisor was [[Thomas Lauritsen]]. [[Nobel laureate]] [[William Alfred Fowler]] also served on his committee.<ref name=r3>{{cite thesis|url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/6614/|title=Beta spectra of the mass 12 nuclei|date=January 1, 1962 |institution=Caltech|degree=Ph.D.|first=F. Curtis|last=Michel|access-date=July 5, 2016}}</ref>

While on the faculty of [[Rice University]], Michel oversaw the dissertations of Jerry Modisette, Robert LaQuey, Robert Manka, Cliff Morris, Michael Pelizzari, Jürgen Krause-Polstorff, James Sokolowski, and Steven Sturner.<ref name=r5>{{cite web|url=http://space.rice.edu/alumni/history.php|title=Department History|date=June 12, 2015|publisher=Rice University|access-date=July 5, 2016|archive-date=June 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160627161038/http://space.rice.edu/alumni/history.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Organizations ==
Michel was a [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]] and a member of the [[American Geophysical Union]], and the [[American Astronomical Society]].<ref name=r4/>

== Experience ==
[[File:PORTRAIT - SCIENTIST-ASTRONAUT GROUP.jpg|thumb|290px|Michel, seated front left, with [[NASA Astronaut Group 4]]]]

Michel was a junior engineer with the [[Firestone Tire and Rubber Company]]'s guided missile division before joining the [[United States Air Force|Air Force]] in 1955. As an [[Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps]] (AFROTC) graduate, he received flight training at [[Pinal Airpark|Marana Air Force Base]], [[Arizona]], and at [[Laredo Air Force Base]] and [[Perrin Air Force Base]] in [[Texas]]. During his three years of military service, Michel flew [[North American F-86D Sabre|F-86D]] interceptors in the [[United States]] and in [[Europe]] ([[England]] and [[West Germany]]).<ref name=r2/> Michel accumulated 1,000 hours flying time with 900 hours in [[jet aircraft]].<ref name=r2/>

Following his tour of active duty in the United States Air Force, Michel was a graduate student and research fellow at the [[California Institute of Technology]], doing [[experiment]]al and [[theoretical]] work in [[nuclear physics]] for Lauritsen and [[Richard P. Feynman]], along with work in [[theoretical astrophysics]] for Fowler.

He joined the faculty of [[Rice University]] in [[Houston]], [[Texas]] in July 1963. Michel's efforts there were directed at researching and teaching [[space sciences]],<ref name=vermontscientist>{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28637697/the_burlington_free_press/|title=Vermont Scientist May Be On Early Mission to the Moon|newspaper=The Burlington Free Press|location=Burlington, Vermont|date=June 28, 1965|page=1|via=Newspapers.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> such as the interaction of the [[solar wind]] with the [[lunar atmosphere]].<ref name=r2/>

Michel was selected as a scientist-astronaut in [[NASA Astronaut Group 4]] in June 1965.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28241336/lebanon_daily_news/|title=Six Young Scientists Become US Astronauts Today at Space Center|agency=UPI|newspaper=Lebanon Daily News|location=Lebanon, Pennsylvania|date=June 29, 1965|page=17|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> He resigned from [[NASA]] on August 18, 1969<ref name="MSC 69-55">{{cite news|title=ANNOUNCEMENT OF RESIGNATION OF ASTRONAUT CURTIS MICHEL|url=https://www.nasa.gov/centers/johnson/pdf/83121main_1969.pdf|access-date=April 24, 2020|publisher=MSC Press Release 69-55|agency=NASA|date=August 5, 1969|archive-date=February 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202120858/https://www.nasa.gov/centers/johnson/pdf/83121main_1969.pdf|url-status=dead}} {{PD-notice}}</ref> without having been assigned to any spaceflight missions. Michel believed that it was his decision to resign (after it became clear that he would not be given a flight assignment) that motivated the scientific community to demand that his fellow scientist-astronaut [[Harrison Schmitt]] be reassigned to [[Apollo 17]] (replacing [[Joe Engle]])<ref name="a17pre">{{cite web|title=A Running Start – Apollo 17 up to Powered Descent Initiation|url=http://next.nasa.gov/alsj/a17/a17.prepdi.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320233958/http://next.nasa.gov/alsj/a17/a17.prepdi.html|archive-date=March 20, 2012|access-date=August 25, 2011|publisher=Apollo Lunar Surface Journal}}</ref> after Schmitt's planned mission on Apollo 18 was cancelled.<ref name="RiceU Obit">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Mike |date=July 17, 2009 |title=From astrophysicist to astronaut — and back |url=http://news.rice.edu/2009/07/17/from-astrophysicist-to-astronaut-and-back/ |access-date=June 10, 2021 |publisher=Rice University News & Media |quote=Michel contends that if he had not resigned when he did, Harrison "Jack" Schmitt — the only one in Michel's astronaut class to walk on the moon — might never have done so. "Jack wasn’t even on the agenda," he said. "Another guy was scheduled (for Apollo 17), but the National Academy of Sciences got all pushed out of shape when I left. I think that was largely influential in Jack getting his flight. When it looked like their primary idea of getting a scientist to the moon was going to flop, they finally started pushing their weight around." |archive-date=July 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718060632/http://news.rice.edu/2009/07/17/from-astrophysicist-to-astronaut-and-back/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After his resignation from NASA, Michel returned to teaching and research at Rice, where he also served as chair of the [[space physics]] and [[astronomy]] department from 1974 to 1979.<ref name=r1/> He was the Andrew Hays Buchanan Professor of [[Astrophysics]] from 1974 until his retirement in 2000. Michel was named a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] to the [[École Polytechnique]] in [[Palaiseau]], [[France]], from 1979 to 1980, and was awarded a [[Humboldt Prize]] to study in [[Heidelberg]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]], in [[West Germany]], from 1983 to 1984. Following his retirement, Michel spent the 2001–2002 academic year in [[Japan]] at the Solar-Terrestrial Environment Laboratory of the [[University of Nagoya]] as a visiting professor.<ref name=r4>{{cite web|url=http://psr.rice.edu/bio.html|title=Curt Michel Biographical Sketch|publisher=Rice University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402144336/http://psr.rice.edu/bio.html|archive-date=April 2, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Michel's research spanned many disciplines. In 1964, he predicted the existence of spin "optical rotation" due to [[parity (physics)|parity]] nonconserving [[weak interactions]].<ref name=r7>{{cite journal |last1=Michel|first1=Curtis|journal=Physical Review|title=Parity Nonconservation in Nuclei|date=January 27, 1964|volume=133|issue=2B|pages=B329–B349|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.133.B329|bibcode=1964PhRv..133..329M}}</ref> This phenomenon was experimentally confirmed in 1980 and is used to study parity nonconserving weak interactions between [[neutrons]] and [[Atomic nucleus|nuclei]].<ref name=r8>{{cite journal |title=Parity violation effects in neutron scattering and capture|journal=Lettere al Nuovo Cimento|volume=28|issue=16|pages=538–540|last1=Forte|first1=M.|doi=10.1007/BF02772925|date=August 1980|s2cid=123277597}}</ref> Michel is best known for his work on [[pulsars]] and [[neutron star]] magnetospheres<ref name=r6/> but his work also included [[solar wind]] interactions with the [[Moon]] and other bodies, extending to the [[heliopause (astronomy)|heliopause]]. In 2000, Michel officially retired from Rice but he continued to be active in research until his death in 2015.<ref name=r5/>

== Books ==
* Michel is the author of the book ''Theory of Neutron Star Magnetospheres'', University of Chicago Press, 1990 {{ISBN|9780226523316}}.<ref name=r6>{{cite book |url=http://www.press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/T/bo3641575.html|title=Theory of Neutron Star Magnetospheres|date=November 15, 1990|isbn=9780226523316|last1=Michel|first1=Curtis|publisher=University of Chicago Press}}</ref> 
* Michel is the author of the book ''Handbook of High-Energy Astrophysics Experiments'', Springer Verlag, 2015 {{ISBN|9781441965288}} .
* Michel was a contributor to the book ''NASA's Scientist-Astronauts'' by David Shayler and [[Colin Burgess (author)|Colin Burgess]], Springer Praxis, 2007 {{ISBN|9780387218977}}
